clue.text: Device to prevent slippage is protecting male climber

indicators.note: the first piece wraps round the next as if guarding it

parts.note: a cleat is a projection on a shoe or deck that stops slipping
taken as written

explanation.surface: A non-slip gadget is shielding a man who climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The clematis is a familiar garden vine that scrambles up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Chicken cooked longer will get hot inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within the other
cooking alters ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A bird cooked for longer will be hot through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes LEGORN from LONGER, and 'inside' puts H within it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of domestic chicken originally from the Italian port of Livorno.

clue.text: Showing concern about drug being psychedelic

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: minding means caring or showing concern
blow is slang for cocaine or cannabis

explanation.surface: Caring about drugs that cause hallucinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing concern' wants to be the definition; it is the container, and 'psychedelic' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychedelic experiences are literally overwhelming to the mind, hence the term.

clue.text: Spent time with one socialist

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a red is a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A socialist has spent time in someone's company.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted or worn out describes someone whose energy is spent.

clue.text: Friend's turned up with book I needed for exam documentation

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: an ally is a friend, with the possessive giving the S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend arrives with a book the speaker needed for exam papers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' means the word is read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlines of course content for examinations are set out in these documents.

clue.text: Keep mum in prison

definitions.meaning: to keep mum is to stay silent, as a command to be quiet does
locked away or confined, as a prisoner is

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a curt order to be silent and a description of someone locked up.

clue.text: Marshbuck: a kind of antelope that is — not hard to rear

indicators.note: in a down clue to rear means to stand upright, read from the bottom

parts.note: a gnu, or wildebeest, is an antelope

indicators.note: not hard means the H, for hard as on pencils, is removed

explanation.surface: A marsh antelope is a type that is easy to raise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H from THAT IS, giving TATIS; 'to rear' turns A GNU TATIS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitatunga is an African swamp antelope, also known as the marshbuck.

clue.text: Queen's, Belfast, for example: posh, its location

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
NI is Northern Ireland, where Belfast stands

explanation.surface: Queen's in Belfast is a smart place, and here is where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen's University Belfast is in Northern Ireland, NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen's is a university, and uni is the casual short form.

clue.text: Customer's second order still on the table?

definitions.text: Customer's second order still on the table?

parts.words: Customer's second order still on the table?
parts.note: food that a diner ordered yet left untouched stays sitting on the plate

explanation.surface: A diner's second request is still under negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the table' suggests a proposal under discussion, but here it is food literally left on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left uneaten remains on the table after the meal.

clue.text: The British went all out to make this succeed

definitions.text: The British went all out to make this succeed

parts.words: The British went all out to make this succeed
parts.note: 'all out' means on strike, every worker downing tools, as happened across Britain in 1926

explanation.surface: The nation made a supreme effort for some great success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All out' reads as maximum effort, but it is the cry calling every worker out on strike; the 1926 nationwide stoppage needed everyone out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage involving workers in all industries needs everyone to walk out at once.

clue.text: Banned, because unwelcome

parts.note: for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'
bad news is unwelcome news

explanation.surface: Something was prohibited because nobody wanted it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old spelling of the past tense of forbid, meaning prohibited.

clue.text: Cure's new version of Tainted Love

indicators.note: a new version reworks the material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: The band The Cure has recorded a cover of the song Tainted Love.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cure and Soft Cell's 'Tainted Love' make a pop-music picture; 'new version of' rearranges TAINTED plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that counteracts a poison is the classic sense of this word.

clue.text: Grade that can make a difference

definitions.meaning: the highest grade or class in an exam or degree
a distinguishing feature or contrast between two things

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a top exam grade and a difference marking things apart.

clue.text: A pub with good cheer? That's an original

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is a round of hearty applause and cheering

explanation.surface: A lively, cheering pub is something truly unique.
explanation.definitionFit: Something new and never done before, a novelty, is an original creation.

clue.text: Inspection copy includes old record

indicators.note: includes means the piece takes another inside it

parts.note: an audit is an official inspection of accounts
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: A review copy of a book contains an old recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic tape holding sound is a recording medium, here used as a noun.

clue.text: Louis XIV maybe suffered decline

parts.note: Louis XIV was called the Sun King, his emblem being the sun
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king, completing the Sun King

explanation.surface: The French monarch perhaps went into a decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis XIV's nickname, the Sun King, is shortened with K standing for king.
explanation.definitionFit: Having gone down or fallen low, in the past participle, is what this word describes.

clue.text: Prepare to fly out team of volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
XI is eleven, the size of a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A squad of volunteers gets ready to leave by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft move along the ground to the runway before take-off, preparing to depart.

clue.text: Still a tortuous climb to get round peak of Everest

indicators.note: getting round means surrounding the next piece
tortuous means twisting, so these letters are rearranged
peak of means the top, or first letter, of the word

explanation.surface: A winding ascent still has to go around the summit of Everest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortuous' makes ALMBIC from A CLIMB; 'to get round' puts E, from 'peak of Everest', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling apparatus, a kind of still.

clue.text: Being only partly dressed, pretty girl's liable to become flustered

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: being flustered means being jumbled up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A half-dressed beauty is likely to get embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' as a pretty girl is dated British slang; the definition sits at the front of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-derived word names a state of undress or casual, partial attire.

clue.text: Flashy lights in street South York Do rigged up

clue.text: Hannibal takes new stand

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the cannibal in The Silence of the Lambs

explanation.surface: The Carthaginian general takes up a fresh position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannibal' suggests the general, but it is the fictional Dr Lecter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a reading stand for a speaker's notes or a church Bible.

clue.text: I go in shivering, draped in short, jaunty bathrobe

indicators.note: draped in means wrapped inside the following piece
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: pert means lively and jaunty

indicators.note: shivering suggests shaking about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shivers on entering, wrapped in a short, cheerful dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram's fodder includes the first 'in'; the second 'in' belongs to the container signal 'draped in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose dressing gown worn by women, especially after bathing, is this French garment.

clue.text: Two months needed to prepare herbal extract

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
Oct is the abbreviation for October

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy takes two months to make.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil down a plant material to extract its essence is to make a decoction.

clue.text: Group of splendid stars performed in the days of yore

definitions.text: performed in the days of yore

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cluster of brilliant stars shone in ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: Didst is the archaic second-person past of do, so it means performed in olden speech.

clue.text: Volume turned up on the radio, late in the day

definitions.text: Volume turned up on the radio, late in the day

parts.words: Volume turned up on the radio, late in the day
parts.note: a volume is read aloud each night on a long-running BBC Radio 4 programme of evening readings

explanation.surface: Someone turned the radio volume up late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like loudness, but it is a book, which 'turned up' on air in an evening slot.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a nightly radio reading from a novel, broadcast near bedtime.

clue.text: Blade slicing head off pig

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a boar is a male or wild pig

explanation.surface: A knife cuts the head off a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar is its blade, and rowers call oars blades.

clue.text: English and French scientist coming together as a team

parts.note: Pierre or Marie Curie, pioneers of radioactivity in Paris

explanation.surface: An English and a French researcher join forces in a single group.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing this French word names a stable or team of cars and drivers.

clue.text: Stamps leaseholder put next to seal, half obscured

indicators.note: half obscured means only half of the word remains visible

parts.note: a tenant holds property on a lease

explanation.surface: A tenant attaches a partly hidden seal to a document.
explanation.walkthrough: Se-tenant is a philatelic term from French, 'holding together'.
explanation.definitionFit: Philatelists use this French term for stamps of different designs printed joined together.
